(Today through Sunday)...
Issued at 301 AM EDT Mon Sep 14 2026

A brief break from the warmer weather comes today as high pressure 
in tandem with a quick moving upper trough within the band of 
westerlies will move into New England by this evening. Upper ridging 
will expand back north into the Ohio Valley by Tuesday with a 
resumption of hot and humid conditions through midweek along with a 
periodic threat for thunderstorms as a frontal boundary becomes 
quasi-stationary over the lower Great Lakes. The ridge will persist 
over the southeast U S through the weekend with the front drifting 
into the area during the second half of the week before retreating 
back north. Above normal temperatures will continue for much of the 
period with slightly cooler air holding off until early next week.

Today through Wednesday Night

Clear skies early this morning as Canadian high pressure has taken 
over across the region. With dewpoints into the 50s and northeast 
winds...comfortable temperatures at 06Z ranging from the mid 50s to 
the mid 60s. 

The presence of the high as it moves east from the Great Lakes into 
New England by this evening will produce a brief break from the 
warmer weather experienced much of the first half of September so 
far. The heat and humidity however will return in earnest as early 
as Tuesday with return flow on the back side of the departing high 
advecting a hot and humid airmass back into central Indiana through 
midweek.

A notable area of deep subsidence will accompany the high pressure 
today and pivot across the northeast half of the forecast area. This 
will aid in a spectacular day highlighted by sunny skies...much 
lower humidity levels and cooler temperatures. Diurnal cu will be 
limited to the lower Wabash Valley primarily where afternoon 
humidity levels will be subtly higher. As mentioned...this is 
temporary with the hot and humid airmass suppressed to the south 
drawing back into the area Tuesday as ridging aloft expands into the 
Ohio Valley Tuesday. 

A cold front will track into the Great Lakes and mid Mississippi 
Valley on Tuesday. A broad area of convection will develop this 
evening over the upper Midwest aided by a strong low level jet and 
accompany the boundary as it drifts south into Tuesday morning. 
There does appear to be potential for convection and remnant cloud 
debris to make it as far south as the northern Wabash Valley prior 
to the weakening of the 850mb flow during the morning hours 
otherwise expect much of the day will be dry for the forecast area. 
By late day...the remnant outflow boundary from the complex tonight 
and early Tuesday may serve as a focus for renewed convection within 
a highly unstable airmass across the northern half of the forecast 
area. A capping inversion will be present south of Interstate 70 
where mainly sunny and hot conditions will persist. Model soundings 
show steep lapse rates through 700mb with DCAPE values over 1000 
j/kg. A lack of BL shear will keep convection pulsating in intensity 
but stronger cells will carry a damaging wind risk that will last 
into the evening. 

The front will slip into the northern half of the forecast area 
Tuesday night and Wednesday with the potential for periodic storms 
overnight Tuesday then again Wednesday afternoon and night as subtle 
waves aloft ripple through the region. With PWATs in the 1.75 to 2 
inch range and ample instability in place...convection will carry a 
risk for locally heavy rainfall and gusty winds.

Temps...low level thermals today support highs ranging from the mid 
70s northeast to the lower 80s in the lower Wabash Valley with 
comfortable humidity levels. Highs will recover into the low and mid 
90s Tuesday with heat indices around 100 degrees in the afternoon. 
Temperatures for Wednesday are more conditional and are dependent on 
convective coverage. Have highs ranging from the upper 80s north to 
mid 90s south but if the boundary can make it further south and 
there are more clouds and storms...daytime temperatures will end up 
lower.

Thursday through Sunday

The Ohio Valley will remain in between the strong upper ridge to the 
south and the band of westerlies to the north...resulting in the 
frontal boundary retreating back north at the end of the week as 
heights aloft rise yet again. Convection will largely be isolated 
and diurnally driven both Thursday and Friday. A sharper upper level 
wave will track across the northern tier of the country this weekend 
suppressing the ridge back to our south. Consequently the front will 
be pulled back south into the forecast area as well with an increase 
in clouds and scattered convection. 

Temperatures will range from the mid 80s to lower 90s for much of 
the area Thursday through Saturday falling back into the lower and 
mid 80s as the boundary drops into central Indiana on Sunday.
